official_measurement_examples.name: Planning route distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK guidance states planning permission may be required for demolition and, where full permission is not required, prior approval can still be required before demolition.

official_measurement_examples.name: Part 11 prior approval
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK guidance explains that qualifying demolition can be permitted development under Part 11 subject to conditions including possible prior approval of demolition method and site restoration.

official_measurement_examples.name: 50 cubic metre rule
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK guidance states demolition of a building under 50 cubic metres is outside development for the identified 2021 demolition direction context, subject to other consent regimes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Conservation area distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK guidance applies stricter demolition controls in conservation areas and identifies cases requiring planning permission or specific Part 11 treatment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Listed and scheduled separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK guidance explains ordinary planning permission or prior approval is not the controlling route for listed buildings or scheduled monuments, where separate consent regimes apply.

official_measurement_examples.name: Demolition and EIA
official_measurement_examples.fact: GOV.UK EIA guidance states demolition works can constitute a project for EIA purposes and may require screening where significant environmental effects are possible.

official_measurement_examples.name: Building Act notice control
official_measurement_examples.fact: Local-authority guidance applies Building Act sections 80 to 83 to demolition controls and identifies section 80 notice duties subject to statutory exceptions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Redevelopment separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A redevelopment planning permission can address demolition in the planning scheme, but separate Building Act and other statutory demolition duties can still apply.

core_rules: planning permission for demolition is distinct from Building Act section 80 notice
section 80 demolition notice is not planning permission
planning prior approval for demolition is not section 80 notice compliance
permitted development demolition is not unconditional demolition authority
Part 11 Class B conditions must be checked for the actual building
prior approval application is not prior approval grant
prior approval grant is not section 81 demolition specification
section 81 local authority notice is not planning refusal
section 82 appeal or court process is distinct from planning appeal
section 83 statutory undertaker obligations are distinct from planning permission
under-50-cubic-metre exception must not be treated as a general no-consent rule
50 cubic metre threshold is not parcel redevelopment capacity
conservation-area demolition controls are distinct from ordinary demolition outside conservation areas
listed building demolition is controlled by listed-building consent rather than ordinary demolition planning permission
scheduled monument demolition is controlled by scheduled monument consent
absence of ordinary planning permission requirement is not absence of other consent
redevelopment planning permission does not automatically satisfy Building Act demolition notice duties
section 80 notice compliance does not authorise redevelopment
demolition method approval is not redevelopment planning permission
site restoration prior approval is not future land-use permission
EIA screening is not planning permission
EIA screening not required is not demolition approval
EIA requirement can change the planning route and must be evidenced
unsafe-building circumstances must not be assumed from vacancy
urgent safety demolition exception must be evidenced
building rendered unsafe by interested person action can affect permitted development availability
listed status must be checked before demolition
scheduled monument status must be checked before demolition
conservation area status must be checked at the demolition date
pub or drinking-establishment demolition restrictions must be checked against current law
demolition of a wall or enclosure has separate scope rules and must not be inferred from building rules
demolition of statues memorials or monuments has specific controls
115 cubic metre monument threshold is not a general building demolition threshold
10-year monument period is not a planning permission duration
planning condition on demolition is not section 80 notice
section 80 notice is not environmental permit
demolition waste permit or exemption is distinct from demolition planning permission
asbestos management duties are distinct from demolition planning permission
utility disconnection is not demolition approval
adjacent occupier consultation is not planning consent
statutory undertaker consultation is not landowner consent
demolition boundary is not Land Registry title boundary
demolition permission does not transfer ownership
historic demolition approval must not be applied to a different structure
source decision and demolition dates must be preserved
NO_DATA must remain NO_DATA rather than no demolition constraint
no parcel demolition clearance redevelopment outcome or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research confidence is not parcel demolition-control accuracy
